question: How are Goodenough's (1992) PMc > Chuukese vowel changes entered?
chosen_reading: As rows of Chuukese against Proto-Chuukic (Goodenough's PTk, which keeps the PMc vowels and the central [ɨ] of *u as ɨ, as Jackson's 1984 rows have it), derivation composed. Sequences of unlike vowels that became double vowels (§2.3.1) are entered as cluster rows on both members (V1 > VV / _+V2, V2 > VV / V1+_); 'in some cases' is sporadic; changes stated as one of two outcomes have conditioning unknown. Vowel length is IPA ː; Goodenough's ú é á ó are ɨ ə æ ɔ as in Goodenough & Sugita (1980). The Kiribati and Woleaian statements, made against POc, are entered against their parents (PCMC, PCK).
alternatives: Enter only the single-vowel changes (§§2.3.2-2.3.6) and leave §2.3.1 and the final-vowel loss to the notes.
